stories.body: Iran said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed despite a reported agreement involving an Oman route, while Donald Trump said mines had been cleared from international waters and warned that any ships laying new mines would be destroyed. Inside Iran, pressure is growing to end the conflict as officials and analysts warn that the strait cannot remain a permanent source of leverage: Gulf states are pursuing alternative pipelines and export routes, potentially weakening its strategic value, while sanctions, an oil-export blockade and budget pressures are weighing heavily on Iran's economy.
stories.headline: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz remains closed despite an Oman route deal

stories.body: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on roughly C$28 billion worth of US goods, including steel, dairy products, furniture, tuna and cotton T-shirts, after the Trump administration imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian imports following the collapse of trade talks. The measures, due to take effect on 8 September, are intended to match the US levies, and Ottawa will also provide C$7.5 billion in support for affected businesses and workers. The White House said Canada had rejected preferential market access, while Trump threatened further tariffs on Canadian automobiles.
stories.headline: Canada imposes retaliatory tariffs on US goods as its trade war with Washington escalates

stories.body: CIA Director John Ratcliffe reportedly made an unannounced visit to Moscow, his first known trip to Russia as the agency's chief. Flight-tracking data showed a US military C-17 flying from Latvia to the Russian capital, and US media reported that Kyiv had been asked to pause long-range strikes while a senior US delegation was there. Neither the CIA nor the White House commented on the purpose of the trip, which comes as US-brokered talks to end Russia's war in Ukraine have stalled and could also concern detainee exchanges or wider escalation management.
stories.headline: CIA Director John Ratcliffe reportedly visits Moscow as Ukraine peace talks remain stalled

stories.body: At least 15 newborns were killed after a fire broke out in the nursery of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad, according to local media and hospital officials. Sixteen newborns were reportedly in the ward and only one was rescued. Officials said the fire may have begun when an air-conditioner compressor exploded; the blaze was extinguished and an investigation was ordered. Police said the badly burned victims would need to be identified through DNA testing before their bodies could be returned to their families.
stories.headline: At least 15 newborns die in a hospital fire in Pakistan

stories.body: President Donald Trump has sent a classified civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review. The agreement is intended to support Riyadh's nuclear programme, but remains contingent on Saudi Arabia normalising relations with Israel.
stories.headline: Trump submits a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress

stories.body: Dan J. Sullivan, a retired teacher who shares the name of Alaska's Republican senator, Dan S. Sullivan, advanced from the state's top-four primary to November's ranked-choice Senate election. He will appear alongside the incumbent and former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola in a race that could help determine control of the Senate. The challenger won a court fight to get on the ballot after state officials initially argued that his candidacy was intended to confuse voters; he will be listed as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., with no party affiliation.
stories.headline: A second Dan Sullivan advances to Alaska's general-election Senate ballot

stories.body: Former Oklahoma state senator Mike Mazzei narrowly won the Republican runoff for governor over Attorney General Gentner Drummond, aided by Donald Trump's endorsement, substantial self-funding and outside spending. Mazzei loaned his campaign $11.6 million and the Club for Growth spent about $8 million supporting him and attacking Drummond. He will face Democratic state Representative Cyndi Munson in November and is heavily favored in a state Trump won by 34 percentage points in 2024.
stories.headline: Trump-backed Mike Mazzei wins Oklahoma's Republican primary for governor

stories.body: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested 49,571 people in July, the highest monthly total of Donald Trump's second term, according to agency data obtained and analyzed by the Deportation Data Project. The figure was 15% higher than June's total and 70% above February's. The administration has shifted from highly visible operations in major cities to tactics including arrests at traffic stops, expanded cooperation with state and local agencies, and enforcement against Haitians who have lost deportation protections; local law-enforcement partners accounted for about 6,500 arrests in July.
stories.headline: ICE arrests rise to nearly 50,000 in July, the highest monthly total of Trump's second term

stories.body: Spain's government has begun work on a new asylum law and a reform of the immigration law that would align the country with the European migration pact and speed up the handling of protection claims and returns. The proposed asylum process would resolve some cases within three months, while people arriving irregularly who do not qualify for protection could face returns within 12 weeks. The plans are still at an early stage and require consultation, parliamentary approval and further legislation, but come amid an unprecedented migration crisis in Ceuta.
stories.headline: Spain moves to tighten asylum and immigration laws amid the Ceuta migrant crisis

stories.body: Spain's defence minister, Margarita Robles, said the intelligence service alerted police, the Civil Guard and the government's Ceuta delegation on 29 July to a call for migrants to enter by swimming the following day. Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said no intelligence or police report had forecast an arrival on the scale that followed, and the Ceuta delegation said it had received no warning of the events. The conflicting accounts exposed coordination tensions within the government as it responds to the border crisis, in which more than 140 people reportedly died near the Tarajal breakwater.
stories.headline: Spanish ministers dispute whether intelligence services warned of the mass migrant arrival in Ceuta

stories.body: Spain's cabinet approved a decree creating a mandatory, public electronic register for people and organisations seeking to influence central-government decisions. Managed by the Council for Transparency and Good Governance, the register will oversee compliance and impose sanctions. Senior officials, advisers and trusted staff will have to disclose meetings and contacts with registered interest groups within a month, while a legislative footprint will document lobbyists' involvement in drafting laws and public policies. The decree must be ratified by Congress within 30 days.
stories.headline: Spain creates a national public register of lobbyists by decree

stories.body: A wildfire in the Collserola Natural Park, in Barcelona's Nou Barris district, burned about 35 hectares and prompted the preventive confinement of Torre Baró and Ciutat Meridiana because of smoke. Authorities evacuated 35 residents from homes closest to the forest, while more than 200 firefighters and aerial units worked on the blaze. The fire was stabilised overnight, although crews continued monitoring its perimeter and secondary hotspots; it also disrupted roads, buses, metro stations and local rail service.
stories.headline: A wildfire in Collserola forces evacuations and the confinement of two Barcelona neighborhoods

stories.body: Barcelona plans to transform the former La Escocesa textile complex in Poblenou into a mixed-use creative, social and economic hub by the end of 2029. The project, with a minimum investment of €51.8 million, would renovate 11,528 square metres and include 72 adapted homes and support services for people with disabilities and other vulnerable residents, an inclusive arts centre, studios for artists, a social-economy hub and the Barcelona FoodLab food-technology incubator. The city will provide €27.2 million, with the remainder expected from partner institutions, the third sector and businesses.
stories.headline: Barcelona plans a €51.8 million redevelopment of La Escocesa into housing, cultural and innovation spaces by 2029

stories.body: Catalonia's agriculture minister, Òscar Ordeig, said authorities could assess this autumn whether to begin easing restrictions on access to natural areas, including Collserola, if the African swine fever outbreak continues to improve. He welcomed the first week without positive cases among captured wild boar but said the outbreak is not over and that restrictions will not be relaxed until experts endorse it and sanitary clearance work is complete.
stories.headline: Catalan authorities say they may ease African swine fever restrictions in Collserola this autumn if the outbreak continues to improve

stories.body: Catalonia's Cybersecurity Agency has warned of a new type of hybrid scam that combines online deception with physical deliveries, such as packages containing QR codes that lead to fraudulent websites. Officials said criminals use multiple contacts, including messages and calls impersonating banks, to create urgency and make scams seem credible, while artificial intelligence has made fraudulent messages harder to identify. The agency advises people to pause before acting, avoid clicking links or responding impulsively, and verify urgent requests through an independent channel.
stories.headline: Catalonia warns of a new hybrid scam model combining digital fraud with physical deliveries
